lesson: Card #3 went 1W-1L for -$8.26. Wrexham drew instead of winning — a reminder that "hard to beat" cuts both ways. West Ham's win at Bolton landed as expected. Today we've leaned harder into goals and double-chance markets rather than only straight wins, since two of today's three English matches had a clearer statistical case for goals than for a specific winner.

matches.analysis: FEATURED MATCH. Twente's straight win price (around 1.30) is too short to offer real value — backing heavy favourites at that level barely covers the risk. The better angle is goals: Twente have scored 9 goals in their last 3 games but concede at a rate of roughly 1.25–1.4 per game themselves, while Telstar have found the net in 3 of their 4 league games this season and score consistently away from home. Their last head-to-head meeting finished 1-1. Both attacks are live; neither defence is fully trustworthy.

matches.match: Derby County vs West Bromwich Albion
matches.analysis: Four of the last five head-to-head meetings between these two have produced goals at both ends, and six of West Brom's seven games this season have seen both teams score. Derby (20th, just above the relegation zone, beaten 3-0 by West Ham last time out) are leaking goals, while West Brom (5th, three wins from five) are scoring freely. The win market is muddled by Derby's decent home head-to-head record despite poor current form — the goals market is the cleaner read.

Norwich's home form has been streaky (wins and losses alternating across their last seven), and Birmingham have drawn four of their last seven — a defensively disciplined away side, not an easy one to break down. Norwich are priced as clear favourites at around 1.91, but that price doesn't reflect how tight this fixture actually looks on the numbers. No side offers backable value at the current price. Pass.

Both sides are level on 10 points and playing well, which makes a straight winner hard to call with confidence — but QPR are missing three first-team attackers to injury (Chair, Dembélé and Kemper among them), which meaningfully blunts their threat on the road. Charlton have won four of their last five at The Valley. Rather than force a straight win pick either way, the safer read is Charlton avoiding defeat, which the double chance price covers at a reasonable return.
